messages:
jamal: FYI escalated ticket from Acme SRE — they're seeing intermittent TLS/502 errors when calling our dedicated endpoint via their corporate proxy (BlueCo). Happens only through their proxy, direct outbound ok. Any quick ideas?

diana: Do we have packet captures or client logs? CONNECT should tunnel TLS, so either proxy is actually MITMing (terminating TLS) or they're doing some weird header munging before tunnel.

alex_acme: pasted a few snippets from our tests. repro steps we ran:

curl -v --proxy http://proxy.blueco.corp:8080 https://dedicated.acme.redwood.ai:443  
* About to connect() to proxy.blueco.corp port 8080...
* Connected to proxy.blueco.corp (10.10.10.5) port 8080 (#0)
> CONNECT dedicated.acme.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1
> Host: dedicated.acme.redwood.ai:443
> Proxy-Authorization: Basic REDACTED

< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established
* CONNECT phase completed
*  0.00.0s TLS handshake, 
* SSL: no shared cipher
* Closing connection 0

and sometimes: 
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, ClientHello (1)
* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* server certificate verification OK

but on failures we see 'handshake failure' and client aborts.

maria-support: Thanks Alex — can you also share an s_client capture? If the proxy is intercepting and re-terminating TLS it will present its CA or rewrite SNI. If SNI gets changed to an internal name we see routing issues.

alex_acme: ran a tcpdump of the TLS ClientHello hitting our edge and extracted the Server Name extension. Snippet below (hex->ascii):

ClientHello SNI: "blueco-inspect.internal"
ClientHello SNI: "dedicated.acme.redwood.ai"

so sometimes the SNI presented to our edge is their inspection hostname (blueco-inspect.internal). Looks like their gateway is terminating the client TLS then opening a new TLS to us with SNI set to their inspection box — i.e., full TLS interception.

kyle: That matches a TLS-inspecting proxy doing MITM. Two behaviors to note: (1) if they re-initiate TLS to us and set SNI to an internal name, our TLS routing (SNI-based vhost/certificate selection) will be wrong and cert mismatch / handshake errors can occur. (2) If the proxy reuses an upstream pool socket across different downstream clients, SNI might get mixed.

jmal: (typo) jamal: Rephrase — Kyle yes. Also explains flakiness. Sometimes their proxy passes full tunnel (SNI intact) -> success. Sometimes their inspection farm handles connection -> SNI rewritten -> fail or wrong cert.

diana: Workarounds we can propose to customer: 
- Ask BlueCo to add your domain to a TLS-passthrough/allowlist so CONNECT is pure tunnel (recommended).
- Add our endpoint to their proxy egress allowlist by IP (bypass MITM). We can provision an ephemeral static IP for testing.
- Try an alternate port (e.g., 8443) as some enterprise filters only intercept standard 443.
- Long term: Dedicated static IP (Private/Dedicated) so customers can allow that IP.

jmal: Also possible short-term trick: have them set the proxy to tunnel mode for that destination, or set PAC rules to bypass for *.redwood.ai.

eng-ops-bot: Escalation created: INC-2026-0421, priority P2. Assigned: eng-runtime (kyle), support (maria-support).

kyle: I'll provision an ephemeral test IP and enable extra SNI logging on the edge to confirm SNI values for incoming TLS. If we can prove the SNI is rewritten we can show BlueCo security team the evidence.

jmal: Thanks all. Alex — once you have confirmation from BlueCo about passthrough or allowlist we can move to close. For now I'll mark status = waiting on customer. :thumbsup:

alex_acme: Alex — can you run a quick smoke test against our alternate endpoint on 8443? Command:

curl -v --proxy http://proxy.blueco.corp:8080 https://alt-test-ephemeral.redwood.ai:8443 -H "Host: dedicated.acme.redwood.ai" --tlsv1.3

(we're asking them to try Host override to force HTTP Host header in case their proxy meddles with it; for CONNECT the Host header is only in the HTTP CONNECT line but some corporate proxies rewrite headers for proxied requests)

alex_acme: running now. Results: 8443 via proxy -> consistent success. 443 still fails ~30% of connections. When it fails our edge logs show SNI=blueco-inspect.internal; when it succeeds SNI=dedicated.acme.redwood.ai.

diana: That is a smoking gun — the proxy intermittently terminates client TLS and re-initiates to us with the inspection hostname as SNI. Recommend customer ask BlueCo to add a TLS passthrough rule for dedicated.acme.redwood.ai or allowlist our ephemeral IP.

maria-support: I'll send the customer-facing note with repro steps and the two immediate mitigations (1 — request passthrough from BlueCo, 2 — we provide ephemeral IP to allowlist). Also mention alternate port 8443 as a short-term workaround.

kyle: Action items for eng: (A) provision ephemeral IP for Acme test and share it in the ticket; (B) enable SNI logging for 12h and attach PCAPs; (C) consider adding a fallback route that uses client certificate or IP-based binding when SNI is missing/rewritten (RFC: fallback is nontrivial but we can prototype).

jmal: Thanks all. Alex — once you have confirmation from BlueCo about passthrough or allowlist we can move to close. For now I'll mark status = waiting on customer. :thumbsup:

alex_acme: thanks — will update after talking to BlueCo security.
